info.title: TwitterAPI.io over Airnode
info.description:
TwitterAPI.io serves X (Twitter) data over a plain HTTP API with a single key, without the approval the official API asks for. This Airnode wraps its read endpoints, so a consumer receives a profile, a tweet or a search result with a signature saying this Airnode obtained it from TwitterAPI.io at this time.

X data is worth attesting because it moves and then disappears. A tweet is edited or deleted, a follower count is only true for an instant, and an account is suspended: a signed answer says what the platform returned while it was still there, which is a claim a screenshot cannot make.

Only reads are wrapped. TwitterAPI.io also posts, likes, follows and sends messages on behalf of a logged-in account, which is acting rather than reporting, and none of it is something an attestation makes more trustworthy.

Every response carries an EIP-191 signature from the Airnode that served it, so the data can be attributed back to its source rather than trusted on reputation.

get.description: Describes the operations this Airnode serves and how to verify what it returns. Free.

200.description: An OpenAPI document describing this Airnode.

post.summary: Perform an operation and attest to the response.

operation.description: The profile behind a handle: follower and following counts, the bio, when the account was created, whether it carries a blue check, and whether it is suspended or otherwise unavailable. The counts are the reason to attest one, since they are true only at the moment of the call.

userName.description: The handle, without the leading @. This is the name in the profile URL rather than the display name.

responseProjection.description: Optional. Maps a name of your choosing to an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response, such as {"price": "/ethereum/usd"}. data is then the text of a JSON object of those names in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it, instead of the whole body, and the projection is part of the signed request identity. No two names take the same pointer, and no pointer is inside another's value. A pointer the response does not have is a 400.

oneOf.description: What one account posted most recently.

operation.description: The account's own timeline, newest first, up to 20 tweets a page. Replies are left out unless asked for, so what comes back is what the account published rather than what it said to somebody else.

userName.description: The handle, without the leading @. This is the name in the profile URL rather than the display name. The upstream also accepts a numeric account id instead, which this Airnode does not wrap: it takes one or the other, and a document cannot say that about two parameters it has called optional.

oneOf.title: searchTweets
oneOf.description: Search tweets, with X's own query syntax.

operation.description: The full search grammar rather than a keyword box: from:, to:, since_time:, until_time:, min_faves: and the rest compose in one query string, which is what makes this the operation for a question nothing else answers. Up to 20 tweets a page.

query.description: The search, in X's query syntax. Quoted phrases, OR and the from:, to:, since_time: and min_faves: filters all compose.

queryType.description: Which ranking to search under. Latest is reverse chronological, Top is what X considers most relevant.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous page. Omit it for the first page.

oneOf.title: trends
oneOf.description: What is trending in one place.

operation.description: The trending list for a location, ranked. Trends turn over through the day, so an attestation over one says what a place was talking about at that moment, which is a claim that cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

woeid.description: The Where On Earth id of the place: 1 is worldwide, 23424977 the United States, 2418046 a city. Not a country code.

200.description: The upstream response and the attestation over it.

400.description: The operation exists but the parameters or the projection are missing, unknown or malformed, a path parameter is empty, . or .. or has such a part between slashes, or the projection names too many fields, an empty or repeated pointer, or a path the response does not have. Also a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header that does not decode to a payment payload.

402.description: The operation is paid and no valid payment was supplied. The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header carries the x402 payment requirements to retry against.

502.description: The upstream API could not be reached or refused the request.

airnode.description: The address whose signature attests to this response.

requestHash.description: Identifies the request this response answers.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds at which the response was signed.

data.description: The upstream response body exactly as received, less a leading byte order mark. With a projection, the text of a JSON object keyed by the names it asked for in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it.

attestation.digest: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes32 requestHash, uint256 timestamp, bytes dataBytes))
attestation.requestHash: keccak256(utf8(JSON.stringify([operation, parameterEntriesSortedByName]))), where an object value is itself entries sorted by name, at any depth, and an array keeps its order. Names are compared by Unicode code point. A request that carries a projection appends its entries, sorted the same way, as a third element
attestation.verify: Recover the signer of the signature over the digest and check it equals the address above.

parameters.x-airnode-sign: false skips the signature: no attestation headers, and the body streamed through with no size cap.
parameters.x-airnode-project: alias:pointer, once per field to keep and at most 20 times, each pointer an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response that starts with /, is not repeated and is not inside another's value. The body becomes an object of those aliases in Unicode code point order, the signature covers it, and a pointer the response does not have is a 400.

passthrough.flow: Send the request the provider documents, method, path, query and body as they are, to url followed by the route's path. The body comes back as the upstream sent it, with the upstream's status, and on success the attestation is in the X-Airnode-Address, X-Airnode-Request-Hash, X-Airnode-Timestamp and X-Airnode-Signature headers, with the operation served in X-Airnode-Operation. Every query parameter starting with x-airnode- is this Airnode's own, listed under parameters, and never reaches the upstream.
passthrough.requestHash: keccak256(utf8(JSON.stringify(["passthrough", method, path, queryEntries, headerEntries, body]))), where method is upper case, path is what was sent after url as a URL parser resolves it, the query entries are what was sent with the Airnode's own parameters removed, in the order sent, headerEntries are the headers that the routes declare as parameters and the request sent, each name in lower case and sorted by Unicode code point, with the values of a header sent more than once joined with ", " in the order sent and the result trimmed of spaces and tabs, and body is the request body as sent, or an empty string. A request that carries a projection appends its entries, sorted by name in Unicode code point order, as a seventh element
passthrough.dataBytes: UTF-8 of the response body exactly as received, less a leading byte order mark, or of the projected object

payment.flow: An unpaid call to a priced operation returns 402 with the x402 payment requirements, base64-encoded, in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. Sign an EIP-3009 authorization matching one entry and retry the call with the payment payload, base64-encoded, in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. The settlement receipt comes back in the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header.
